questions.prompt: Explain what Copy-on-Write (COW) is in Swift. In 2 to 5 sentences, describe how it balances performance with value semantics.

rubric.criterion: Explains that COW is an optimization where value types share underlying heap storage until mutation
Notes that it preserves value semantics by copying the buffer only when one variable modifies the data

questions.modelAnswer: Copy-on-write is an optimization in Swift where multiple value types share the same underlying storage buffer after an assignment. No memory is duplicated while the data is only read, which makes copying O(1) in time and memory. When one of the variables mutates the data, Swift duplicates the buffer first. This provides the performance of reference types while preserving strict value semantics.

sources.title: The Swift Programming Language: Structures and Classes

questions.prompt: Do custom Swift structs have Copy-on-Write behavior automatically? In 2 to 5 sentences, explain what happens when a custom struct is copied.

rubric.criterion: Clarifies that custom Swift structs do not have copy-on-write automatically
Explains that copying a custom struct copies all stored properties directly on the stack

questions.modelAnswer: Custom Swift structs do not have copy-on-write behavior automatically. When you assign or copy a custom struct, Swift immediately copies all of its stored properties. Only standard library collections like Array, Dictionary, Set, and String have built-in COW. If developers want copy-on-write behavior in a custom struct, they must implement it manually.

questions.prompt: How do you implement custom Copy-on-Write in a Swift struct? In 2 to 5 sentences, describe the role of isKnownUniquelyReferenced.

rubric.criterion: Explains that the struct wraps a private reference class holding the actual data buffer
Explains that mutating methods call isKnownUniquelyReferenced to check reference count and copy the buffer if shared

questions.modelAnswer: To implement custom copy-on-write, a struct wraps a private class instance that holds the underlying data on the heap. Before any mutating operation, the struct calls isKnownUniquelyReferenced passing its private storage. If the function returns true, the mutation happens in place because no other instance shares it. If it returns false, the struct allocates a new class instance with duplicated data before writing.

questions.prompt: Why can holding a reference in a closure cause unexpected Copy-on-Write duplication during collection mutations? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Explains that capturing a collection in a closure creates an additional reference to the underlying storage buffer
Notes that isKnownUniquelyReferenced detects a reference count greater than 1, forcing a deep copy on mutation

questions.modelAnswer: When a collection is captured in a closure or stored in another variable, its underlying storage buffer reference count increases to two or more. If code then mutates the collection while the closure is still alive, the collection's uniqueness check detects multiple references. Because the buffer is shared, Swift forces a full memory copy before the mutation occurs. This can cause unexpected performance drops in tight loops.

questions.prompt: How does passing a collection as an inout parameter optimize memory performance compared to passing and returning a value? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Explains that inout passes a reference to the existing variable without incrementing storage reference count
Notes that isKnownUniquelyReferenced remains true, allowing in-place O(1) mutations without COW allocations

questions.modelAnswer: Passing a collection as an inout parameter passes the existing storage reference without creating an additional copy. Because no second reference exists, the underlying storage remains uniquely referenced with a count of one. Any mutations performed inside the function happen in place without triggering a COW duplication. In contrast, passing by value and re-assigning can create temporary references that trigger redundant deep copies.
